name: level3-playthrough-win
description: Level 3 (Treranium Depths): 3 surveys and one real 24-hole blast against a mine that is already legally bankrupt before it fires -- named for an $800k win across 5 patterns (184 holes) with all 10 hired employees dying, but `campaign start level:treranium_depths` fails outright (locked, Findings #58/#59/#61/#62) and #553's queued, vehicle-gated drilling breaks the rest of the premise for real. staffed:true's free driller+drill_rig, stacked on top of this file's own 10 hand-hires and 5 hand-bought vehicles (15 employees, 9 vehicles total against a $220,000 budget), burns through the bankruptcy threshold before a single hole lands: 'BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized.' fires at tick 139, 271 ticks before pattern 1's 24 holes -- drilled for real by 2 concurrent driller/drill_rig pairs -- finish landing at tick 410 (#596/#597: retimed from tick 400 by the idempotent event pool and cached cooldown-threshold fixes). The pattern blasts for real anyway (nothing halts a tick or a blast once levelEnded flips): PERFECT rating, 1,507 m3 cleared, 11 of 15 employees dead, 6 of 9 vehicles destroyed. One real contract cycle (accept + storage-empty delivery refusal, via #597's `type:rubble_disposal` stable contract selector) follows; patterns 2-5 (160 more holes, 4 more explosive types) are dropped entirely -- see the final campaign status step for the full measured trajectory.

The mine is seized.' fires at tick 139 -- 271 ticks before this pattern finishes drilling and long before blast 1 ever fires. Nothing in the engine stops a `tick` command from continuing to run a level after levelEnded flips (a genuinely pending EVENT is the only thing that ever halts one), so the mine keeps operating -- legally seized, crew still working -- for the rest of this file. bankrupt/levelEnded/levelEndReason are this file's new real conclusion, first observable here now that the fields are in scope. #591: cash updated -387412->-387190 -- the staffed fleet's spawn spacing widened (SPAWN_TILE_SPACING, GameState.ts) and EntityMovementTick.ts now wires in VehicleOccupancyReroute.ts's stuck-detection/reroute, shifting exact vehicle-pathing/payroll timing without changing tickCount/holeCount or the bankruptcy outcome.

CI finding, this PR (#586): was role: player (issue #515) driving real clicks through the Charge step. It can't be -- `state.bankrupt` flipped true (and levelEndReason to 'bankruptcy') two tick-blocks back, and `LevelEndScreen.update()` (src/main.ts:526, called after every command whenever `!tutorial.isActive`) shows its full-screen `#bs-level-end-screen` overlay -- `position:fixed;inset:0` at `--bsx-z-menu` -- the instant `levelEndReason` goes non-null, for EVERY defeat reason, not just worker_revolt. It stays up: `update()` only clears `rendered` (and re-hides) when `levelEndReason` goes back to null, which a defeated level never does. So `#bs-blast-panel [data-step="2"]` is exactly the covered-by-div failure this PR's other broken scenario files hit for a different reason (crew walkout) -- same overlay class, different trigger. The command still runs (nothing in the engine gates a command on `levelEndReason`, matching this file's own established 'nothing halts a tick or a blast once levelEnded flips' narrative below) and chargedCount still reaches 24 -- only the UI path to get there is gone. `role: guard` + `expect.blocked` proves that honestly instead of asserting a click no real player could make.

#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing. #601-followup: dropped the speed-button click that used to precede this wait -- it was only ever needed to make the OLD real-time-driven `waitUntil` (auto-tick loop, real wall-clock) advance faster; #601's harness fix replaced that with a loop of the console's own synchronous `tick 1`, which never reads `state.timeScale` at all, so the click has done nothing since #601 landed. It became actively harmful here rather than merely dead: the charge step just above is itself a `role: guard` proving `state.bankrupt` already flipped level-end (see its own note), and `LevelEndScreen`'s full-screen overlay covers the whole page including the HUD the instant that happens -- so `awaitUsable` on the speed button could only ever time out once the level-end timing (already accepted as real and covered, upstream) lands before this step instead of after it.
Same #bs-level-end-screen overlay as the Charge step above -- see its description. Was role: player driving a click through the Sequence step; converted to guard for the same reason.

#553/#554: this file's real 24-hole pattern (the pre-#553 file's own already-corrected grid, Finding #52) is violent enough (PERFECT rating, 1,507 m3 cleared) to kill 12 of the 15 employees on site -- a direct trace shows all 10 of this file's own hand-hires (employees #6-15) dead, plus employee #1 (Gus Rubble, the free staffed driller) and employee #2 (Walt Rockwell, the free staffed blaster), both of whom spent hundreds of ticks physically working this pattern (drilling, then #554's real queued charging). The only 3 survivors are staffed:true's remaining free hires (#3-5: the 3 staffed drivers), who never went anywhere near the pattern. 6 of the file's 9 vehicles are destroyed too: the free staffed drill_rig (#1) and all 5 of this file's own hand-bought vehicles (#5-9), which were parked squarely inside the drill pattern's footprint the whole time. CI finding, this PR (#586): was role: player driving the execute/confirm/report-close click sequence -- same `#bs-level-end-screen` overlay as the Charge and Sequence steps above blocks `#bs-blast-panel [data-step="5"]` (and everything downstream of it) from the moment bankruptcy fires. The blast still detonates for real (command mode and this guard step's own `command` interaction agree on every number above) -- the automated systems, not a player's click, are what fire it, matching this file's own 'legally seized, crew still working' framing. Converted to guard rather than pretending a confirm dialog could be clicked through a full-screen game-over overlay.

wellBeing already at its floor (11 deaths' morale hit) -- safety/ecology still the fresh-game baseline here, same reasoning as tutorial-playthrough.json's own post-blast scores step: the recentAccidents/vibration penalties only start applying once ticking resumes.

Sandbox-measured: a genuine pending EVENT (lucky_strike) is already queued the instant this tick call starts, so it advances 0 of the 6 requested ticks -- tickCount and cash are unchanged here, resolved by the event choose 0 step below.

Resolves lucky_strike (+$10,000, a fixed cash bonus -- same event type noted in level1-win-efficient.json/level2-playthrough-win.json). CI finding, this PR (#586): was role:player driving `resolveEventIfPending`'s real click -- state.levelEndReason has read 'bankruptcy' since tick 139 (271 ticks before this step), and the event dialog's own overlay class (`.bs-confirm-overlay`, EventModal.ts) sits at z-index 600, far below `--bsx-z-menu` (9999) that LevelEndScreen's full-viewport overlay has owned since then -- same class of bug as the Charge/Sequence/blast steps above, just on a dialog instead of a panel. Every earlier 'event choose 0' step in this drilling wait stays role:player safely because `resolveEventIfPending` no-ops (no click at all) when nothing is genuinely pending; this is the one step in the file where an event (lucky_strike) really is pending at the moment it runs, so it is the one step that actually reaches `resolveEventIfPending`'s bare `page.click('#bs-event-dialog .bs-event-choice')` -- which has no `describeUnclickable` wrapper, so Puppeteer's own unnamed 'Node is either not clickable or not an Element' surfaced instead of a diagnosis. Converted to guard + expect.blocked, command run directly so the $10,000 still lands.

#597: switched from a numeric id (contract accept 19) to the stable `type:rubble_disposal` selector (`ContractSelector`, `Contract.ts`; `parseContractSelector`, `economy.ts`) -- REFRESH_INTERVAL rotates the offer pool on its own clock, and this file's 410-tick drilling wait (up from 400 pre-#596/#597) already once knocked id 19 off the specific contract this step meant (it now names a 410kg 'Deliver rustite ore' offer, not the rubble-disposal one this step is about). `type:rubble_disposal` names the offer by what it actually is, so a future pacing shift moves which id it lands on without renumbering this file again. Verified via a real run: at tick 410 it resolves to contract #20 (Dispose of rubble, 160kg) -- the first rubble_disposal offer `contract list` above holds. CI finding, this PR (#586): was role: player, scoped to `[data-contract-id="19"] .bs-contract-accept` (#513/#581, so command mode and interaction mode couldn't silently accept different contracts) -- converted to guard for the same `#bs-level-end-screen` reason as the Charge/Sequence/blast steps above: `#bs-toolbar [data-panel="contracts"]` itself is covered by the full-screen bankruptcy overlay, so not even opening the panel is reachable, let alone the accept button inside it. The command still runs and activeContractCount still reaches 1 -- the pool refresh and the auto-negotiation systems that make this contract exist don't care about the UI any more than the blast does.

BLOCKED, and deliberately not converted to a click: the ACTIVE card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled -- ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together whenever maxDeliverable = min(contract remaining, stored material) is 0, and a direct trace shows 0.0 kg stored (storedMassKg never leaves 0 anywhere in this file -- both debris_haulers this file buys are destroyed in the blast above, and the free staffed debris_hauler (#2) is never driven either). amount:160 matches the accepted contract's own quantityKg (#20, Dispose of rubble); the console command still caps to whatever's actually owed and returns success:false ("Not enough stored material: 0.0 kg available, 160.0 kg requested.") -- command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so this is a silent no-op in both modes. `expect.blocked` pins it down instead of asserting something the game correctly forbids. Same `type:rubble_disposal` selector as the accept step above (#597) -- `deliver`'s own resolveContract call matches it against `state.contracts.active`, which holds the same contract #20 accept just put there, so both steps stay pointed at the same contract without hardcoding its id twice. CI finding, this PR (#586): originally also asserted `usable: "#bs-contract-panel [data-action=\"goto-ops\"]"` -- dropped, because that control is covered by the same `#bs-level-end-screen` bankruptcy overlay as everything else on this page from the Charge step onward (see its description); nothing on the page is usable once levelEndReason goes non-null, so that assertion could never have passed and the original 'BLOCKED, deliberately not converted to a click' framing already had the right instinct without knowing why the panel itself was gone too. #554 follow-up (real interaction-mode CI finding): id 20 itself drifted again -- REFRESH_INTERVAL keeps cycling the offer pool and this file now spends more real ticks getting here (the driller/charging changes above), so the hardcoded numeric id from the #597 fix is exactly the moving target that fix already diagnosed for the accept/deliver console commands, just still present in this one CSS selector. Switched to data-contract-type (ContractsPanel.ts, added alongside data-contract-id for exactly this reason) the same way the console commands above already use type:rubble_disposal, instead of renumbering the id again.

expect.note: #553/#554: this file's real conclusion, retimed by #596/#597 (idempotent event pool + cached cooldown threshold shift when the pending event becomes true) and again by #554 (charging is now real queued work, not instant). Named for an $800,000 win across 5 patterns (184 holes total) and all 10 hired employees dying; `campaign start level:treranium_depths` fails outright (tier-3, locked, unchanged from Findings #58/#59/#61/#62), so the run plays out on the substitute new_game world throughout. Under #553's queued, vehicle-gated drilling, staffed:true's free 5-person/4-vehicle composition stacked on this file's own 10 hand-hires and 5 hand-bought vehicles (15 employees, 9 vehicles total, $220,000 budget after $165,000 of that goes straight into the fleet) can no longer survive even the first drilling wait: 'BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized.' fires at tick 139, 271 ticks before pattern 1's 24 holes (drilled for real by 2 concurrent driller/drill_rig pairs -- the free staffed rig plus a hand-hired driller licensed into this file's own idle drill_rig) finish landing at tick 410. Nothing halts a tick or a blast once levelEnded flips, so the mine keeps operating -- legally seized, crew still working. #554: charging is now real queued work too -- the same drillers load all 24 holes' charges over ticks 410-460 before the blast fires. Pattern 1 blasts for real anyway at tick 460: PERFECT rating, 1,507 m3 cleared, and kills 12 of the 15 employees on site -- all 10 of this file's own hand-hires (employees #6-15) plus employee #1 (the free staffed driller) and employee #2 (the free staffed blaster), both of whom worked the pattern through drilling and charging; only staffed:true's 3 drivers (#3-5) survive -- while destroying 6 of the 9 vehicles: the free staffed drill_rig and all 5 of this file's own hand-bought vehicles, all parked squarely inside the pattern's footprint. One real contract cycle follows (accept + a storage-empty delivery refusal, both via #597's `type:rubble_disposal` selector against contract #20 -- storedMassKg never leaves 0; every debris_hauler in play is either destroyed in the blast or, like the free staffed one, never driven). Patterns 2-5 (36+30+30+64 = 160 more holes, the remaining 4 explosive types) are dropped from this file entirely: narrating drill_plan cycles for a mine that is $428,440 in the hole, has 3 employees left, and no fleet capable of drilling or hauling anything would document nothing real -- same resolution level3-playthrough-ecology.json already used for its own unreachable patterns 3-6. cash is exact and reproducible (fixed seed, command-mode measured, no wall-clock dependency); bankrupt/levelEnded/levelEndReason are the file's real ending, not the named $800k target. #554: tickCount moved from 410 to 460 and cash from -377190 to -428440 -- the 50 extra ticks of real queued charge-loading (also killing employee #2, the staffed blaster, who was drilling-then-charging alongside employee #1 at blast time) add payroll/upkeep on top of #591's own -377412->-377190 drill-wait retiming, without changing the bankruptcy outcome.
